testCase.question: Does this section prove that HCR requires a vanity in the bathroom?
testCase.expectedConclusion: No. In its Type B+NYC unit toilet-and-bathing-room context, the selected Building Code subsection establishes the required water-closet clearance when only a forward approach is provided and permits a compliant lavatory at the specified rear-wall location. A lavatory and a vanity must remain distinct: this subsection does not establish an HCR vanity requirement, and its permissive lavatory-location language does not prove that no other Building Code provision requires a lavatory. Confirm whether the unit and bathroom are subject to the Type B+NYC provisions and provide the applicable HCR design standard, program or funding requirement, or official agency guidance before stating what HCR requires.

expectedUncertainty.description: The answer must state directly that the selected Building Code passage cannot establish an HCR requirement and request applicable HCR authority.

answer.answerText:
No. This NYC Building Code section does not prove that HCR requires a bathroom vanity.

The cited forward-approach provision applies only where a water closet has only a forward approach. It requires specified water-closet clearances and says that a lavatory complying with another section is **permitted** on the rear wall at a stated distance from the water-closet centerline.  Permitted  allows that location; it does not require a lavatory, and it does not require a vanity, cabinet, countertop, or storage.

Separately, within the stated scope of a Type B+NYC dwelling or sleeping unit, the NYC Building Code requires at least one compliant lavatory in each provided toilet or bathing room. That is a NYC Building Code lavatory requirement—not an HCR requirement—and the supplied text does not equate a lavatory with a vanity. The Type B+NYC scope and the forward-approach layout have not been established here.

To determine whether HCR itself requires a vanity, the applicable HCR regulation, program design standard, funding or regulatory agreement, or official agency directive is needed.
answer.conclusion: No. This NYC Building Code section does not prove that HCR requires a bathroom vanity.

supportedPoints.heading: Forward-approach rule permits, but does not require, a lavatory location
supportedPoints.explanation: Where only a forward approach is provided to a water closet, the provision requires 66 inches of clearance measured from the rear wall and 48 inches measured from the side wall. It then states that a lavatory complying with Section 1107.2.2.5 is permitted on the rear wall, at least 18 inches from the water-closet centerline. This is placement permission, not a mandate to install a lavatory or a vanity.

supportedPoints.heading: The broader NYC rule requires a lavatory only within its Type B+NYC-unit scope
supportedPoints.explanation: Where toilet or bathing rooms are provided in a Type B+NYC dwelling unit or sleeping unit, the provision requires at least one compliant lavatory and water closet in each toilet room; in each bathing room, it requires at least one compliant lavatory, water closet, and either a bathtub or shower. It does not use or define a vanity requirement. This scope is not established by the supplied project facts.

citations.title: 1107.2.2 Type B+NYC unit toilet and bathing rooms.

supportingPassages.selectedText: 1107.2.2 1107.2.2 Type B+NYC unit toilet and bathing rooms. Where toilet and bathing rooms are provided in a Type B+NYC dwelling unit or sleeping unit, all such toilet and bathing rooms shall comply with Sections 1107.2.2.1 through 1107.2.2.9. Within each such toilet room, at least one lavatory, and one water closet shall comply with Sections 1107.2.2.1 through 1107.2.2.7. Within each bathing room, at least one lavatory, one water closet, and either a bathtub or shower shall comply with Sections 1107.2.2.1 through 1107.2.2.8. Toilet and bathing fixtures shall be in a single room, such that travel between fixtures does not require travel beyond the room in which the fixtures of such toilet or bathing room is located. Additional fixtures shall comply with Section 1107.2.2.9. Exception for Type A toilet and bathing room: Where at least one toilet and bathing room complying with Sections 1003.11 (Toilet and Bathing Facility) and 1003.3.2 (Turning Space) of ICC A117.1 is provided within a Type B+NYC dwelling unit or sleeping unit in accordance with Items 1 through 3 of this exception, other toilet and bathing rooms in the same unit shall be required to comply only with Sections 1004.3 (Accessible Route), 1004.4 (Walking Surfaces), 1004.5.2 (User Passage Doorways), 1004.9 (Operable Parts) and 1004.11.1 (Grab Bar and Shower Seat Reinforcement) of ICC A117.1. In addition, a vertical grab bar 18 inches (457.2 mm) minimum in length shall be mounted with the bottom of the bar located between 39 inches (990.6 mm) and 41 inches (1041.4 mm) above the floor, and with the center of the bar located at 30 inches (762 mm) from the rear wall. Doors and doorways to such toilet and bathing rooms shall be subject to Section 1107.2.1, Exception 5. 1. At least one lavatory, one water closet and either a bathtub or shower within such toilet or bathing facility shall comply with Section 1003.11 of ICC A117.1. Such toilet and bathing fixtures shall be in a single toilet or bathing area, such that travel between fixtures does not require travel beyond the area in which the fixtures of such toilet or bathing room are located. 2. Toilet paper dispensers within such rooms shall comply with Section 604.7 (Dispensers) of ICC A117.1. 3. Medicine cabinets, if provided, must include a storage shelf no higher than 44 inches (1117.6 mm) above the floor. (Am. L.L. 2023/077, 6/11/2023, eff. 6/11/2023) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2023/077 .

controllingProvisions.label: NYC Building Code § 1107.2.2.7.2.2 — Forward approach
controllingProvisions.summary: For a water closet with only a forward approach, this provision requires specified water-closet clearances (66 inches from the rear wall and 48 inches from the side wall). It says that a compliant lavatory is “permitted” on the rear wall at least 18 inches from the water-closet centerline. “Permitted” authorizes that placement; it does not require either a lavatory or a vanity. The provision is part of the Type B+NYC-unit toilet/bathing-room requirements, so it applies only if that parent scope applies.

generalRules.label: NYC Building Code § 1107.2.2 — Type B+NYC unit toilet and bathing rooms
generalRules.summary: Where toilet or bathing rooms are provided in a Type B+NYC dwelling or sleeping unit, the section generally requires at least one compliant lavatory and water closet in each toilet room, and at least one compliant lavatory, water closet, and bathtub or shower in each bathing room. This is a lavatory requirement within the stated accessible-unit scope—not a requirement for a “vanity,” and not an HCR requirement.

generalRules.label: NYC Building Code §§ 1107.2.2.7 and 1107.2.2.7.2 — Water-closet clearance scope
generalRules.summary: The water-closet provisions require compliance with the enumerated water-closet and clearance subsections, including the pinned forward-approach provision where its facts are met.

exceptions.label: Type A toilet-and-bathing-room exception within § 1107.2.2
exceptions.summary: If the detailed Type A-compliant facility described in the exception is provided within a Type B+NYC unit and all listed conditions are met, other toilet and bathing rooms in that unit have reduced compliance obligations. The supplied record does not establish that this exception applies to the project.

conditions.label: Forward-approach condition
conditions.summary: The 66-inch by 48-inch clearance rule applies where only a forward approach is provided to the water closet. The lavatory placement language applies only as a permission within that layout condition.

conditions.label: Type B+NYC unit condition
conditions.summary: The parent toilet/bathing-room fixture rules apply where the room is provided in a Type B+NYC dwelling unit or sleeping unit.

28-104.8.2 § 28-104.8.2 Owner statements. The application shall contain a signed statement by the owner, and, in the case of cooperative or condominium forms of ownership, the application shall also contain a statement by the cooperative or condominium board, affirming that the applicant is authorized to make the application and, if applicable, acknowledging that construction and related documents will be accepted with less than full examination by the department based on the professional certification of the applicant. Such statement shall list the owner's full name and address, as well as the names of the principal officers, partners or other principals if a corporation, partnership or other entity. Principal officers of a corporation shall be deemed to include the president, vice presidents, secretary and treasurer. Where a current deed holder with a valid property interest or a court appointed entity or equivalent in charge of the property, or in the case of a cooperative or condominium unit, the cooperative or condominium board, notifies the department in writing that the applicant does not have authority to make the application, the department is authorized pursuant to section 28-104.2.10 to revoke approval of construction documents. In addition, the application shall contain the following: 1. A signed statement certifying whether the building to be altered, constructed or demolished contains one or more occupied dwelling units; 2. A signed statement indicating whether the building to be altered, constructed or demolished contains housing accommodations subject to rent control or rent stabilization under chapters 3 and 4 of title 26 of the administrative code or rent regulation under article 7-C of the New York state multiple dwelling law; and 3. If the building to be altered, constructed or demolished contains occupied housing accommodations subject to rent control under chapter 3 of title 26 of the administrative code, the application shall contain a signed statement indicating that the owner has notified the New York state division of homes and community renewal that the owner has complied with all requirements imposed by the regulations of such agency as preconditions for such filing; or that the owner has not notified such agency because the nature and scope of the work proposed, pursuant to such regulations, does not require notification; or, if the building is subject to article 7-C of the New York state multiple dwelling law, the application shall contain a signed statement indicating that the owner will notify the loft board of the filing of the construction documents and will comply with all requirements imposed by New York state multiple dwelling law article 7-C and the loft board's rules. (Am. L.L. 2019/106, 6/8/2019, eff. 3/8/2020; Am. L.L. 2021/126, 11/7/2021, eff. 11/7/2022) Editor's note: For related unconsolidated provisions, see Appendix A at L.L. 2021/126 .
